name: Hodaviah
overview: Hodaviah is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Elioenai according to 1 Chronicles 3:24. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture does not provide additional details or notes about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Hodaviah is a proper name meaning 'give thanks to YHWH,' reflecting a devotional acknowledgment of God's sovereignty. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a theologically rich meaning grounded in Hebrew tradition.
familyAndRelationships: Hodaviah is explicitly recorded as the son of Elioenai, as noted in 1 Chronicles 3:24. Scripture does not provide further information about his family or other relationships beyond this filial connection.
scriptureSignificance: Hodaviah's significance in the biblical narrative lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, emphasizing the continuation of the Davidic line through his father Elioenai. Although little is said about his personal actions or character, his mention in Scripture contributes to the preservation of the Messianic lineage, which is central to evangelical Christ-centered theology.
